paper: Exact Transfer of Bounded Linear Recovery and Relative Weight Hierarchies

claims.statement: Minimum-support lifts over the complete outer functional dual give the exact finite rank-stratified confinement cost; under the explicit outer-distance gate this reduces to the associated relative weight plus the inner dual distance, and growing outer dual distance gives the eventual family form.
Minimum-weight normalized recovery equations of an MDS code span its dual code.
The restricted helper map gives the stated exact sequence for the associated nested code pair.

The associated nested pair is literally the shortening-puncturing pair of the inner dual on the helper coordinates; its dual pair is the shortening-puncturing pair of the inner code, and both are independent of the chosen generator-row basis.
The minimum helper-union size for an internally realizable rank-t demand equals the t-th relative generalized Hamming weight of the associated nested pair.
The relative dimension-length profile equals the maximum recoverable target-message dimension from a helper set of bounded size.

For every survivor set, shortening-puncturing duality identifies the unrecovered target dimension with the relative dimension of the dual nested pair on the failed coordinates; its t-th relative generalized Hamming weight is the minimum number of failures leaving t target dimensions ambiguous.

For a fixed nonzero target-message subspace, an outer code with at least two blocks, and a target block with nonzero outer projection, minimizing prescribed-coset union-support costs over linear maps into the complete outer functional dual gives the exact finite first nonconfined helper cost; minimizing over internally recoverable target subspaces gives the ranked criterion and exact transfer below it.

Ordinary prescribed-coset union-support costs compose exactly by blockwise min-sum substitution under repeated concatenation and satisfy the stated sharp support envelopes; helper-restriction costs together with target images give the target-normalized recursion, and a compatible formula gives the composite dual distance and exact nonconfinement cost while keeping zero and nonzero functional sectors separate.
Under the finite outer gate d(O^perp)>r+1 and N>=2, a fixed internally realizable target subspace has the stated sharp confinement threshold; dual-distance growth gives the eventual family form.

Under the finite outer gate, the uniform rank-t nonconfinement helper threshold is the t-th relative generalized Hamming weight plus the inner dual distance; the same holds eventually in outer families of growing dual distance.

For one target coordinate and any finite outer code with nonzero target-block projection, target-constrained inner coset weights give the exact minimum total weight of a nonconfined concatenated dual word and hence an ungated if-and-only-if transfer criterion at every helper radius.

A construction using a Singer cycle and [k+1,k,2]_q inner codes, with k+1 <= n <= 2k+1, satisfies the exact weighted nonvacuous radius-(n-1) transfer gate although the ordinary outer support-distance gate fails; the [4,3,2]_5, n=5 case is explicit.

Minimizing simultaneous helper cost over target e-sets gives the e-th generalized Hamming weight of the dual code minus e, yields the cooperative-locality lower bound, and gives the least eventual first-nonconfinement cost after adding the inner dual distance.

MDS inner codes have the stated exact formulas throughout the recoverable hierarchy, attain the global ceiling when the helper side spans the message space, and first-rank equality in the global ceiling is rigid.
Suitable outer families transfer bounded recovery equations onto positive-density coordinate classes while preserving global asymptotic bounds.

Below the exact prescribed-coset confinement threshold for every demand, transfer of inclusion-minimal helper supports preserves the bounded service-rate region; the outer-dual-distance and inner inequalities are a sufficient condition and hold eventually in the stated outer families.
Two represented rank-one recovery systems have the same minimum helper cost and different bounded reliability polynomials.
At every quotient rank, equal complete relative-weight hierarchies can have different full-recovery reliability laws.
Different ambient inner-dual realizations of the same abstract nested helper pair can have different confinement thresholds; this is not a generator-row-basis change of one fixed inner code.
The projective-simplex family has the displayed relative-weight staircase and confinement thresholds.
The projective-simplex family has the displayed rank-reliability and Moebius-inversion formulas.
Equality in the first projective helper-cost bound characterizes the simplex column multiset.
